title: History of Life on Earth
seo_title: Grade 10 Life Sciences: History of Life on Earth Worksheets (CAPS)
standard_code: Grade 10 Life Sciences: History of life on Earth
standard_text: The geological time scale; the formation of fossils and methods of dating them; the main events in the history of life (the first cells, the Cambrian explosion, life moving onto land, the age of dinosaurs and of mammals); mass extinctions; South Africa's fossil heritage. (summary of CAPS Life Sciences, Grade 10, Life Sciences: History of life on Earth)
meta_desc: Free Grade 10 Life Sciences worksheets (CAPS): fossils and how they form, dating fossils, the geological time scale, mass extinctions and South African fossils. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Fossils are the remains or traces of past life.
key_sub: The deeper the rock layer, the older it usually is.
body_html:
How to think about it

Fossils form when organisms are buried quickly in sediment, which hardens into rock. Relative dating uses the order of rock layers; radiometric dating uses the half-life of radioactive isotopes to give an age in years. The geological time scale is divided into eras and periods.

Life began as simple cells more than 3,5 billion years ago. Later came multicellular life, the Cambrian explosion, plants and animals on land, the dinosaurs, and finally mammals and humans. There have been five mass extinctions, such as the one that ended the dinosaurs 66 million years ago. The Karoo is famous for fossils of mammal-like reptiles.

Example

Which rock layer is usually oldest?

Layers are laid down in order.

Answer: the lowest layer

Example

Half-life 5 730 years; ¼ of the carbon-14 left. Age?

Two half-lives

Answer: 11 460 years

Common mistakes

  • Thinking all dead organisms become fossils.
  • Thinking humans lived with dinosaurs.
  • Thinking relative dating gives an age in years.

faq.q: Why is the fossil record incomplete?
faq.a: Most organisms decay before they are fossilised, and soft bodies rarely form fossils.

faq.q: Why are the Karoo fossils important?
faq.a: They show the change from reptiles to mammal-like animals and the Permian mass extinction.

items.q: What do 4,4-billion-year-old zircons tell us about early Earth?
c: there was continental crust and probably liquid water very early
Earth had no crust for 2 billion years
items.e: Their oxygen isotopes suggest they formed with water present.

items.q: What does radiometric dating measure?
c: the ratio of a radioactive parent isotope to its daughter isotope, to find an absolute age
the order of rock layers only
items.e: Uranium–lead dating is used for zircons.

items.q: A rock started with 96 g of parent isotope and no daughter. After 4 half-lives, how much daughter isotope is there?
items.e: Daughter = original − parent left = 96 − 6 = 90 g.

items.q: A rock started with 128 g of parent isotope and no daughter. After 5 half-lives, how much daughter isotope is there?
items.e: Daughter = original − parent left = 128 − 4 = 124 g.

items.q: A mineral has 1/8 of its original potassium-40 left (half-life 1,25 billion years). How old is it?
items.e: 1/8 = 3 half-lives; 3 × 1,25 = 3,75 billion years.

items.q: A sample had 128 g of parent and now has 32 g. How many half-lives have passed?
items.e: 128 → 32 takes 2 halvings.

items.q: A sample had 96 g of parent and now has 12 g. How many half-lives have passed?
items.e: 96 → 12 takes 3 halvings.

items.q: A sample starts with 96 g of a radioactive parent. How much parent is left after 3 half-lives?
items.e: Halve 3 times: 12 g.

items.q: A mineral has 1/4 of its original potassium-40 left (half-life 1,25 billion years). How old is it?
items.e: 1/4 = 2 half-lives; 2 × 1,25 = 2,5 billion years.

items.q: A sample starts with 96 g of a radioactive parent. How much parent is left after 2 half-lives?
items.e: Halve 2 times: 24 g.

items.q: A sample had 160 g of parent and now has 5 g. How many half-lives have passed?
items.e: 160 → 5 takes 5 halvings.

items.q: What are the three main types of rock?

items.q: A sample starts with 32 g of a radioactive parent. How much parent is left after 3 half-lives?
items.e: Halve 3 times: 4 g.

items.e: Daughter = original − parent left = 32 − 4 = 28 g.

items.q: Lethabo observes in a cliff: “A worn, uneven surface (an unconformity) lies between two sets of layers.” What can be concluded?
c: The two layers formed at about the same time (an index fossil).

Some rock was eroded away, so part of the record is missing.
items.e: Relative dating uses superposition, cross-cutting features, unconformities, inclusions and index fossils.

items.q: Where did most of the water in Earth's oceans come from?

items.q: Oxygen from microbes reacted with iron dissolved in seawater. How did this change Earth's systems?

items.q: What is residence time?

the time a river takes to reach the sea
